source_citation: Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction, Annex on Chemicals, Schedule 1, as amended by the changes adopted 27 November 2019 and in force from 7 June 2020. Text as published by the OPCW, accessed 2026-08-15.
known_limitations: Schedule 1 also lists saxitoxin and ricin, identified by name rather than by structural family. Not encoded: a structural rule for a protein toxin is meaningless, and an identity rule needs a structure this file does not carry.

Size limits ('C10 or fewer, including cycloalkyl') are applied to the molecule's TOTAL carbon count where they are applied at all. Entries A.3, A.13, A.14 and B.10 carry no carbon limit, because applying one to the total would exclude those entries' own examples -- VX and QL both have eleven carbons. Where a limit IS applied it may over-report and will not under-report.

'Corresponding alkylated salts', which several entries reach, are not matched: an alkylated salt is a quaternary ammonium and so a different structure. Protonated forms are reached, because counter-ions are stripped before an identity comparison.

The 2019 additions (entries A.13 to A.16, in force 7 June 2020) are encoded here and carry that date, and a screen asked about an earlier date withholds them. What no entry here records is repeal or expiry -- the Annex has only ever gained entries -- so a dated screen answers when a rule STARTED applying and would report one since removed as though it still did.

This file cites two official reproductions of the same Annex. Entries A.1 to A.6 quote and cite the Canadian export-control reproduction they were written from; the entries added later quote and cite the OPCW's own text. The two render the Annex differently -- 'equal to or less than C10' against '<=C10' -- and the Canadian page predates the 2019 additions, which is why it could not supply them.

rules.description: O-Alkyl alkylphosphonofluoridates. The P-C bond is the distinction from an ordinary phosphofluoridate: diisopropyl fluorophosphate has the same phosphoryl, fluorine and alkoxy and is NOT Schedule 1.

legal.quote: O-Alkyl (equal to or less than C10, including cycloalkyl) alkyl (Methyl, Ethyl, n-Propyl or Isopropyl) - phosphonofluoridate

of.label: P-alkyl is methyl, ethyl, n-propyl or isopropyl

assumptions: the size limit is applied to total carbon count, not per substituent

rules.description: O-Alkyl N,N-dialkyl phosphoramidocyanidates. The nitrile on phosphorus alongside an amide nitrogen is the identifying combination.

legal.quote: O-Alkyl (equal to or less than C10, including cycloalkyl) N,N-dialkyl (Methyl, Ethyl, n-Propyl or Isopropyl) phosphoramidocyanidates

assumptions: 'alkyl' read as any sp3 carbon substituent
limitations: the schedule restricts the N-alkyl groups to methyl, ethyl, n-propyl or isopropyl; this pattern accepts any sp3 carbon

rules.description: O-Alkyl S-2-dialkylaminoethyl alkylphosphonothiolates. The S-CH2CH2-NR2 arm on a phosphonothiolate is the identifying feature.

legal.quote: O-Alkyl (H or equal to or less than C10, including cycloalkyl) S-2-dialkyl (Methyl, Ethyl, n-Propyl or Isopropyl)-aminoethyl alkyl (Methyl, Ethyl, n-Propyl or Isopropyl) phosphonothiolates

of.label: P-alkyl is methyl, ethyl, n-propyl or isopropyl

limitations: no size limit is applied; the schedule bounds the O-alkyl group at C10

rules.description: The 2-chloroethyl thioether motif shared by the sulfur mustard family.
assumptions: The entry is a heading followed by a list of named sub-items, each with an identifier the text prints. The generic entries in the same part introduce their examples with 'e.g.' and this one does not, so the list is read as the listing rather than as examples of a wider family.
Each identity is resolved from the identifier the entry itself prints, not from its name; the name was resolved separately and agreed in every case (12 of 12 across both entries).
Checked against two official reproductions of the same Annex, which agree on every sub-item and every printed identifier.
limitations: NARROWER THAN THE FAMILY PATTERN THIS REPLACES, deliberately. The former pattern matched the shared structural motif, and so also matched molecules the entry does not list -- measured over 23,432 real structures, 12 were matched on that motif and none of them is a listed sub-item. A structure sharing the motif without being listed is now not matched by this rule, which is what the entry says.

A sub-item's salts and stereoisomers are reached by the engine's policy (counter-ions stripped before comparison; same connectivity matched under the regulation's own isomer wording and reported as such), so those need no entry of their own. An alkylated salt is a different structure and is not reached, as elsewhere in this ruleset.

This rule no longer produces a near miss, because the engine's identity path does not: a structure one feature away from a sub-item is reported by neither a finding nor a near miss here. The family pattern could say 'close to this entry' and an identity list cannot.

The entry is a HEADING followed by an enumeration of named members with CAS numbers, which is not reproduced here. A family pattern is therefore broader than the entry and is marked approximate for that reason.

rules.display_name: Phosphonamidic fluorides with an aminoalkylidene (Schedule 1, A.13)
rules.description: One of the four families added in 2019 and in force from 7 June 2020. The phosphorus carries an alkyl directly; entry A.14 is the same motif with the phosphorus bonded to oxygen instead.

legal.quote: Р-alkyl (H or ≤C10, incl. cycloalkyl) N-(1-(dialkyl(≤C10, incl. cycloalkyl)amino))alkylidene(H or ≤C10, incl. cycloalkyl) phosphonamidic fluorides and corresponding alkylated or protonated salts

assumptions: The quote preserves two oddities of the OPCW's own text: this entry begins with a CYRILLIC capital Er (U+0420) rather than a Latin P, so a search for 'P-alkyl' does not find it, and the 2019 entries use U+2264 where the older entries spell it '<='.

The alkylidene carbon is required to carry a CARBON substituent, which is what separates this entry from A.15 -- there the same carbon carries two dialkylamino groups and the treaty lists it separately.
limitations: The entry's size clauses ('H or <=C10, incl. cycloalkyl', three times) are not implemented. Applying them to the molecule's total carbon count would exclude the entry's own C10 examples, the same reason entry A.3 carries no carbon limit.
'Corresponding alkylated salts' are not matched: an alkylated salt is a quaternary ammonium, a different structure. Protonated forms are reached.

rules.description: The A.13 motif with the phosphorus bonded to oxygen rather than carbon. That single difference is what separates the two entries.

legal.quote: O-alkyl (H or ≤C10, incl. cycloalkyl) N-(1-(dialkyl(≤C10, incl. cycloalkyl)amino))alkylidene(H or ≤C10, incl. cycloalkyl) phosphoramidofluoridates and corresponding alkylated or protonated salts

assumptions: The alkylidene carbon is required to carry a carbon substituent, as in A.13.
limitations: The entry's size clauses are not implemented, for the reason given on A.13.

rules.description: A SINGLE NAMED CHEMICAL, not a family -- the only one of the four 2019 additions that is. Its central carbon carries two dialkylamino groups, which is why A.13's alkylidene family does not reach it and the treaty lists it on its own.
assumptions: Identity resolved from the CAS number printed in the entry, not from its name.

rules.description: Quaternaries and bisquaternaries carrying a dimethylcarbamoyloxypyridine. The entry specifies chain lengths (n=1-8 for the quaternaries, n=2-12 for the bisquaternaries) which are not enforced here.
assumptions: Read as two features together: a dimethylcarbamoyloxy group on a PYRIDINE ring, and the alpha-picolinyl methylene to a quaternary nitrogen that the entry's structures describe ("N-(3-dimethylcarbamoxy-alpha-picolinyl)"). Both of the entry's own examples carry that linkage.

THE SECOND FEATURE WAS A BARE QUATERNARY NITROGEN AT FIRST, and that is too common to pair with anything. It matched no ordinary chemical outright, but it satisfied one of the two predicates, which was enough to report choline, betaine, carnitine, acetylcholine and benzalkonium surfactants as NEAR MISSES to a chemical-weapons entry. Requiring the linkage instead of the charge is what removes them. Same failure as the numeric bound that once made ethanol a near miss to a nerve-agent schedule: a predicate satisfied by half of chemistry carries no information.
limitations: The entry's chain-length ranges (n=1-8 and n=2-12) are not enforced, so a molecule carrying both features with a chain outside those ranges is reported. Over-reports within this family and never under-reports.

of.label: a dimethylcarbamoyloxy group on a pyridine ring
a picolinyl methylene carrying a quaternary nitrogen

rules.description: A binary-weapon component. No civilian use is claimed for this family, which is why no legitimate uses are listed.

legal.quote: Alkyl (Me, Et, n-Pr or i-Pr) phosphonyldifluorides

expression.label: alkyl (Me, Et, n-Pr or i-Pr) phosphonyldifluoride

rules.description: The QL family, a binary-weapon component. A phosphonite is trivalent phosphorus, which is what separates this entry from the phosphonothiolates of A.3.

legal.quote: O-Alkyl (H or <=C10, incl. cycloalkyl) O-2-dialkyl (Me, Et, n-Pr or i-Pr)-aminoethyl alkyl (Me, Et, n-Pr or i-Pr) phosphonites and corresponding alkylated or protonated salts

assumptions: 'Phosphonite' is read as trivalent phosphorus carrying two oxygens and one carbon.
limitations: The 'H or <=C10' size clause is NOT implemented, and could not be as a total-carbon count: QL, the entry's own example, has eleven carbons. Entry A.3 carries no carbon limit for the same reason.
